items: Identify Your Business Structure: Search your state's Secretary of State website to determine whether you registered a formal business entity such as an LLC or corporation.
Identify Your Business Structure: Stop the entity search if you never filed formation documents because you operate as a sole proprietor and file Schedule C on your personal 1040.
Identify Your Business Structure: Count your business owners to determine whether you have a single-member entity or a multi-owner structure that requires different tax treatment.
Identify Your Business Structure: Write your entity type in one sentence such as "I am a single-member LLC taxed as a sole proprietor" and keep this statement with all your tax documents.
File the Correct Tax Forms: File Schedule C as part of your personal 1040 if you are a sole proprietor or single-member LLC because your business income flows directly to your individual tax return.
File the Correct Tax Forms: Submit Form 1065 if you have a multi-member LLC that has not elected S-corp status because partnerships report income at the entity level before distributing to owners.

File the Correct Tax Forms: Complete Form 1120-S if you elected S-corp status for your LLC or corporation because S-corps file a separate return but income passes through to shareholders via Schedule K-1s.

File the Correct Tax Forms: Issue Schedule K-1s to each partner or shareholder after filing Form 1065 or Form 1120-S because every owner must report their share of business income on their personal 1040.

Complete Your Tax Submission: Pay yourself a reasonable salary before taking distributions if you own an S-corp and actively work in the business because the IRS requires salary as a precondition for distribution treatment.
Complete Your Tax Submission: Consult a CPA for detailed guidance if you operate as a C-corporation because corporations file Form 1120 and face double taxation on dividends paid to shareholders.

Complete Your Tax Submission: Place specific numbers in the correct IRS boxes on each form because the agency does not accept spreadsheets and requires income and expenses reported in designated fields.

Complete Your Tax Submission: Sign and submit every form in your stack after reviewing each line entry because the IRS holds you responsible for accurate filing regardless of whether you used an accountant.
